text:
maria: Morning — quick debrief on the warm-snapshot benchmark we ran against dedicated-pool-2. TL;DR: snapshot resume fixes weights fast but KV cache misses create a short latency storm.

ajay: Can you paste the run command and headline numbers?

maria: Sure:
```sh
./bench_run --harness=replay --trace=snapshot-resume --duration=12m --pool=dedicated-pool-2 --load=steady:200qps
```
Summary:
- first-token median (no-snapshot baseline): 85ms
- first-token median (snapshot-resume): 305ms
- KV cache miss rate: baseline 2.1% -> resume 18.7%
- autoscale add-node (50->100): 32s median (no regression)
- GPU kernel init cold-start: 6.1s -> 7.9s on resumed instances
- tail p99 end-to-end: 520ms -> 980ms during the first 90s after resume

sam: That KV miss spike implies we aren't rehydrating the KV index on resume, right? Are we doing lazy-on-access only?

maria: Yep. Snapshot restores model state but marks KV segments as stale; they repopulate on first access which causes the miss storm.

ellen: Did you try the selector v2 kernel hinting during the run?

maria: We did a pair of runs. selector v2 gives ~6% steady-state throughput uplift and reduces p95 ~40ms, but it doesn't eliminate the resume miss spike. It helps jitter in steady state though.

nate: Idea: run an async KV prefetch on resume that samples session manifests and warms active prefixes for N ms before accepting traffic. Even a partial warm can cut the miss storm.

maria: I prototyped that. Config used:
```json
{"prefetch":true,"prefetch_window_ms":5000,"sample_fraction":0.25}
```
With that: miss spike down to 4.3%, first-token median ~140ms, p99 ~650ms. Tradeoff: ~60MB extra GPU memory while prefetch runs.

bench-bot: benchmark results uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/warm-snapshot/2034503210/report.html :white_check_mark:

ajay: Any impact on autoscale/burst credits? If many instances resume simultaneously we could burn credit and create a cascade.

maria: Observed ~+18% burst credit consumption during the first 90s after onramp when we didn't stagger resumes. Staggering resumes by ~2s per instance plus the lightweight prefetch keeps credit use within normal variance.

sam: Also consider preferring selector v2 on resumed instances — it smooths CPU and lowers p95, which helps during the recovery window.

ellen: Action items: 1) implement async prefix prefetch on resume with config flags and guardrails; 2) implement staggered resume orchestration for dedicated pools; 3) run a larger canary (2k qps) with the orchestration and prefetch enabled. I'll make the tickets.

maria: I'll attach the replay logs and the perf flame for the resume step. Links: s3://redwood-bench/warm-snapshot/2034503210/flame.svg and s3://redwood-bench/warm-snapshot/2034503210/replay.log

nate: :thumbsup: Also update Optimize docs with prefetch knobs and recommended defaults.

ajay: Solid. If no objections, schedule the canary tomorrow morning and we'll run the 2k qps with 10% progressive onramp.

maria: No objections from me. I'll post the canary plan in #eng-runtime when it's scheduled.

sam: Thanks, great debrief — nice combination of kernel + caching + orchestration fixes.
